revision: two-page plain-language guide with alternatives and choice rationale

comparisons.reason: UMIK-2 factory calibration stops at 20 kHz; M30 G2 calibration at 32 kHz is unconfirmed. M50 offers a 50 kHz range and individual calibration with our Mac interface.
iD4 can do the basic sound checkout, but has one full-band mic/line input. iD14 gives two for recording the mic and electrical timing reference together.
Original MR4 stops at 20 kHz. MR5 ($349.99) also specifies 40 kHz. MR3 saves $200 and covers our target on paper; 10 ms acoustic tests are still required.
Extech 407766 ($519 listed) also provides a 1 kHz level check. R8090 costs less; both state +/-0.5 dB at 94 dB. R8090-NIST adds a certificate at extra cost.
Equivalent XLR mic cables work. This budget cable connects M50 to the interface; the brand is not essential.
Equivalent balanced 1/4-inch TRS cables work. We need two: one for the speaker and one for the electrical reference.
An existing stable boom stand is fine. This inexpensive model holds the mic at the ear/reference position.
